## Change purpose

Describe the smallest necessary change and the public claim, evidence, or operational state it affects.

## Evidence boundary

- [ ] I did not promote a claim beyond its current evidence class.
- [ ] Project rerun, external rerun, independent implementation, and empirical validation remain distinct where relevant.
- [ ] Negative results, counterexamples, and failure lineage are preserved.

## Power-Reversal gate

- [ ] I checked the change under relevant role reversal (for example founder/reviewer, user/platform, human/AI, sponsor/researcher, current/future maintainer).
- [ ] Increased maintainer/system authority does not silently reduce another party's audit, contest, exit, rollback, or recovery capacity.
- [ ] Safety, efficiency, ownership, intelligence, good intent, or policy were not used as automatic self-exemptions from review.
- [ ] This change does not make the same human repeatedly re-explain or reconstruct information already available in the repository.
- [ ] More irreversible changes received proportionally stronger review and recovery planning.

## Rights and privacy boundary

- [ ] No private research, credentials, KYC, personal/health/family data, or unrelated sensitive material is exposed.
- [ ] No license, ownership, destructive deletion, or other hard-to-reverse rights change is inferred from ordinary maintenance authority.

## Final regression

- [ ] If I were in the affected party's position, I would accept the same rule.
- [ ] Repeating this structure would not systematically concentrate control on one side while concentrating repair cost, dependency, or lost options on the other.

If a box cannot honestly be checked, narrow the change, document the exception, or route it for explicit authorized review rather than treating the exception as normal.
